title: 2018 AMC 12B Problem 19
statement: Mary chose an even \(4\)-digit number \(n.\) She wrote down all the divisors of \(n\) in increasing order from left to right: \(1,\) \(2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(\tfrac{n}{2},\) \(n.\) At some moment Mary wrote \(323\) as a divisor of \(n.\) What is the smallest possible value of the next divisor written to the right of \(323?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(d\) be the next divisor after \(323.\) If \(\gcd(d,323)=1,\) then \(323d\) divides \(n,\) forcing \(n\ge323d\gt323^2\gt9999,\) impossible for a \(4\)-digit number. So \(d\) shares a prime factor with \(323=17\cdot19.\)

Then \(d-323\ge\gcd(d,323)\ge17,\) so \(d\ge340.\) Indeed \(d=340=17\cdot20\) occurs for \(n=17\cdot19\cdot20=6460,\) which is even and \(4\)-digit.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: If the next divisor \(d\) were coprime to \(323,\) then \(n\ge323d\gt9999;\) so \(d\) shares a prime with \(323\)
